description: Helium chapter (2 pp.) of the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025: 2024 salient statistics - estimated Grade-A base price about $14 per cubic meter with producers posting surcharges; the Federal Helium System sold in two lots on January 25, 2024 (about 50 Mm3 of crude helium in total) and transferred to a single company on June 27, 2024; the CHEU purification unit's lease lapsed August 11, 2024 with no agreement by year end; the EU import ban on Russian helium effective September 26, 2024; world production 180 Mm3; US apparent consumption 56 Mm3 of which lifting gas is 18%.

notes: One chapter of a larger annual publication; DOI 10.3133/mcs2025 identifies the whole Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025. This is the chapter research/analysis/helium.py takes its 2024 market constants from (price, US consumption, world production, lifting-gas share, import sources 2020-23: Qatar 40%, Canada 36%, Algeria 10%, Russia 4%) and the source of the substitution sentence quoted in the note: hydrogen 'can be substituted for helium in some lighter-than-air applications in which the flammable nature of hydrogen is not objectionable'. Caveats carried into the note: 2024 figures are estimates ('e'), and footnote 5 says USGS estimated 2024 apparent consumption itself because Census Bureau export data 'were unusually high and may have contained misclassified items'. The chapter gives no age for the Federal Helium System - the '90-year buffer' phrase in research/analysis/helium.md is not from this document.
